metadata.title: Tesla Stock Rises as Musk Teases Potential 'Flying' Roadster Debut

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) shares advanced 1% Friday morning as attention returned to the company's long-delayed Roadster, with a redesigned version potentially set for a reveal as soon as August, according to reports.
The sports car could feature technology intended to create a hovering effect during a demonstration at SpaceX (SPCX) facilities in Texas. Elon Musk has previously suggested the vehicle could incorporate flight-related capabilities, although the final specifications and timing remain uncertain.
Any limited version built around such technology would likely target a small group of buyers rather than Tesla's broader customer base. The vehicle could carry a price reaching well into six figures or higher and may not be designed for normal road use.
Tesla's original Roadster helped establish the company as an electric-car manufacturer. Sold between 2008 and 2012, the model used a modified Lotus Elise platform and offered roughly 200 miles of real-world range, with production totaling about 2,450 vehicles.
Tesla showed a successor prototype in 2017, promising rapid acceleration, a top speed above 250 mph and roughly 620 miles of range. The second-generation model has since faced at least eight delays.
